questions.q: During a site inspection, you notice that the Top Bars of a continuous beam have sagged and are now sitting in the middle of the beam's depth. What is the immediate structural consequence?
o: Thermal Expansion
Positive Moment Failure
Increased Ductility
Negative Moment Failure
questions.n: Top bars are designed to resist tension over supports; if they sag, the lack of reinforcement near the top face leads to cracking and failure under negative moments.

questions.q: Why is 'Segregation' (the separation of rocks from paste) particularly dangerous at the bottom of a Column pour?
o: It improves the curing rate
It increases the fire rating of the base
It helps in plumbing installation
It creates 'honeycombs' that reduce the effective cross-sectional area
questions.n: The base of the column carries the highest axial load; 'rock pockets' reduce the area available to resist crushing, leading to potential failure.

questions.q: If it begins to rain heavily during a slab pour, what should be done with the exposed wet concrete surface?
o: Stop the pour and remove the concrete
Cover it immediately
Mix the rainwater into the concrete
Add more cement to the surface
questions.n: Excess water increases the water-cement ratio at the surface, leading to 'dusting' and very low surface strength.

questions.q: Why should Sea Water never be used to mix or cure reinforced concrete?
o: It changes the color of the concrete
It makes the concrete too heavy
It speeds up the setting time too much
Chlorides attack the protective layer of the rebar, causing pitting corrosion
questions.n: Chlorides penetrate the concrete and oxidize the steel, leading to expansion that cracks the concrete from within.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a 'Drip Groove' under a concrete ledge or canopy?
o: To provide structural reinforcement
To act as an expansion joint
To break capillary action and prevent water from crawling back to the wall
To reduce the weight of the ledge
questions.n: The groove breaks the surface tension of the water, forcing it to drop and preventing moisture damage to the building facade.

questions.q: Under RA 9514 (Fire Code), what is the minimum clear width of an Exit Door for an occupant load of 50 or more?
o: 715 mm
815 mm
915 mm
questions.n: 915 mm (36 inches) is the standard minimum width to ensure safe and efficient egress for 50 or more people.

questions.q: In a building equipped with an approved automatic sprinkler system, what is the maximum allowable Travel Distance to an exit?
o: 30.00 meters
46.00 meters
61.00 meters
75.00 meters
questions.n: The presence of a sprinkler system allows for an extended travel distance of 61.00 meters due to increased safety.

questions.q: What is the Fire Rating required for a firewall located on a property line?
o: 3 hours
2 hours
1 hour
4 hours
questions.n: A 4-hour rating (typically masonry/concrete without openings) is required to prevent fire spread across property lines.

questions.q: Under the Fire Code, what is a 'Dead-End Corridor' and what is its maximum allowable length?
o: A corridor with only one exit; 6.00 meters
A corridor with no exits; 3.00 meters
A corridor with two exits; 12.00 meters
A corridor that leads to a window; 9.00 meters
questions.n: Dead-ends are restricted to 6.00 meters to ensure occupants don't travel too far into a trap during a fire.

questions.q: Why does the Fire Code require doors to 'Swing in the Direction of Exit Travel'?
o: To make it easier for firefighters to enter
To ensure the door closes automatically
To save space in the hallway
To prevent a 'logjam' or crush during a panic
questions.n: If a crowd pushes against an inward-swinging door, they will lock themselves inside; outward swing ensures the crowd's pressure opens the door.

questions.q: Under Article 1723 of the Civil Code, how long is the Architect-of-Record liable if a building collapses due to defects in the plans?
o: 15 years
25 years
5 years
10 years
questions.n: The Architect-of-Record is liable for 15 years from the completion of the building for defects in the plans and specifications.

questions.q: If a building collapses due to Defective Construction Materials used by the contractor, is the Architect still liable?
o: No, unless the Architect was also the owner
Yes, if the Architect failed to exercise due 'Supervision'
Only if the Architect signed the delivery receipts
No, it is strictly the contractor's fault
questions.n: The Architect-of-Record has a duty to report inferior materials; failing to do so makes them shared-liable with the contractor.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between an Architect-of-Record (AOR) and an Architect-in-Charge of Construction (AICC)?
o: There is no difference; they are the same person
The AOR is for government projects only
The AOR is for design; the AICC is for execution and supervision
The AOR is a foreigner; the AICC is local
questions.n: The AOR assumes liability for plans and design, while the AICC is liable for the actual construction and site supervision.

questions.q: Can a Civil Engineer legally sign and seal Architectural Plans under RA 9266?
o: No, it is restricted exclusively to Registered and Licensed Architects
Yes, as long as they have a Master's Degree
Only if no architect is available in the region
Yes, if the project is under 3 stories
questions.n: The Architecture Act of 2004 clearly defines architectural documents as the sole domain of licensed architects.

questions.q: What is the legal penalty for an individual practicing architecture in the Philippines without a valid license?
o: Permanent ban from ever applying for a license
A fine of Php 100k to 5M, and/or imprisonment for 6 months to 6 years
Community service for 12 months
A fine of Php 10,000 and a warning
questions.n: RA 9266 establishes these heavy penalties to deter illegal practice and protect public safety.

questions.q: According to SPP Doc 301, if there is a conflict between the Drawings and the Specifications, which one generally governs?
o: The Drawings
Whichever is more expensive
Whichever was signed first
The Specifications
questions.n: The written word is legally considered a more deliberate and detailed expression of intent.

questions.q: What is a 'Punch List' in the context of project management?
o: A list of all the structural steel used in the building
A list of minor repairs and finishing touches needed before final acceptance
A document used to track structural failures
A list of workers who arrived late
questions.n: The punch list identifies small tasks the contractor must fix before the Architect issues the Certificate of Final Acceptance.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a Penalty and Liquidated Damages?
o: Penalties are only for government contracts
Liquidated Damages compensate for actual losses; a Penalty is for punishment
There is no difference; they are synonymous
Liquidated Damages are paid in materials instead of cash
questions.n: Liquidated damages are pre-agreed estimates of loss due to delay, making them more legally enforceable than punitive penalties.

questions.q: What does it mean when a material is specified as 'Or Equal' in construction documents?
o: The contractor can use any brand they want
The material must be exactly the same price
The material must be from the same country of origin
The architect must approve any alternative brand based on quality and performance
questions.n: It allows for competition, but the Architect remains the final judge of whether the substitute is truly equivalent.

questions.q: What is the 'Defects Liability Period'?
o: The total duration of the construction contract
The time it takes for a building to settle into the soil
The time during design when the architect can make changes
The period after completion where the contractor must fix latent defects
questions.n: Usually lasting one year, this period ensures the contractor corrects issues that appear shortly after handover at no extra cost.

questions.q: Why are Stirrups placed closer together near the ends of a beam compared to the middle?
o: To support the weight of the column
To prevent the beam from expanding thermally
To make the beam easier to lift into place
Because Shear Stress is highest at the supports
questions.n: Shear forces peak at the supports, necessitating more reinforcement to prevent diagonal tension cracks.

questions.q: In a One-Way Slab, in which direction does the main reinforcement (the 'bent bars') run?
o: Parallel to the Short Span
Parallel to the Long Span
Diagonally across the slab
Only around the edges of the slab
questions.n: Loads take the shortest path to the supports, so the main reinforcement must span the short direction.

questions.q: What is the purpose of providing 'Hooks' at the end of rebars in a beam-column joint?
o: To mark where the beam ends
To ensure proper 'Development Length' and anchor the bar
To catch debris during the concrete pour
To provide a place for electricians to hang wires
questions.n: Hooks anchor the rebar into the joint, preventing it from slipping out when pulled during seismic events.

questions.q: Why is a Column failure considered more critical than a Beam failure?
o: Columns are more expensive than beams
Columns are always exposed to the weather
Column failure can lead to progressive collapse of the entire building
Beams are easier to repair while the building is occupied
questions.n: A column supports multiple floors; if it fails, it can trigger a 'house of cards' effect for the whole structure.

questions.q: In structural frame design, what is 'Sway'?
o: The vibration caused by mechanical equipment
The upward movement of the foundation
The lateral (sideways) displacement caused by wind or earthquakes
The bending of a beam under its own weight
questions.n: Sway or 'drift' is the horizontal movement that must be controlled to prevent damage to non-structural elements like glass.
